title: (Goddess) Kali's (sacrificial) Offering (The (Goddess) Kali must be propitiated)

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Then Banda Singh made another revelation, That he had intended to slaughter one lakh and a quarter lives. Since he could not meet the intended target, The balance of those sacrificed offerings needed to be cleared. (1)
lines: Then Banda Singh made another revelation,
That he had intended to slaughter one lakh and a quarter lives.
Since he could not meet the intended target,
The balance of those sacrificed offerings needed to be cleared.

blocks.text: As the Guru2 had intended to offer one crore and a quarter sacrifices, The Khalsa Panth had to clear that backlog of sacrificial deaths. The Goddess Kali would only be satiated and propitiated, After the promised number of (Singhs) were slaughtered in war. (2)
lines: As the Guru2 had intended to offer one crore and a quarter sacrifices,
The Khalsa Panth had to clear that backlog of sacrificial deaths.
The Goddess Kali would only be satiated and propitiated,
After the promised number of (Singhs) were slaughtered in war.

blocks.text: The Goddess Kali failing to be propitiated had destroyed, Prithvi Raj Chauhan even though he had sacrificed twenty five lac soldiers. The goddess Kali was invoked by Prophet Mohammed for initiating his religion, But she devoured prophet's progeny as well (for deficient propitiation). (3)
lines: The Goddess Kali failing to be propitiated had destroyed,
Prithvi Raj Chauhan even though he had sacrificed twenty five lac soldiers.
The goddess Kali was invoked by Prophet Mohammed for initiating his religion,
But she devoured prophet's progeny as well (for deficient propitiation).

blocks.text: Anyone who invokes her without propitiating her fully, Fails to escape her wrath (after partial propitiation). (But) One who invokes her and satiates her sacrificial craving, She bestows prosperity on him as well as on his progeny. (4)
lines: Anyone who invokes her without propitiating her fully,
Fails to escape her wrath (after partial propitiation).
(But) One who invokes her and satiates her sacrificial craving,
She bestows prosperity on him as well as on his progeny.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The Gods had invoked and appeased her in Satyuga3 , Whereupon they had happily witnessed her blessings.
Lord Rama4 had satiated and appeased her in Treta Yuga, Who, along with his whole dynasty, received her blessings. (5)
lines: Lord Rama4 had satiated and appeased her in Treta Yuga,
Who, along with his whole dynasty, received her blessings.

blocks.text: The Pandavas5 invoked the Goddess in the age of Duapar, And offered the sacrificial (blood) to her heart's content. They had satiated and appeased not only the goddess, But her whole progeny as well (with the blood of their brethren). (6)
lines: The Pandavas5 invoked the Goddess in the age of Duapar,
And offered the sacrificial (blood) to her heart's content.
They had satiated and appeased not only the goddess,
But her whole progeny as well (with the blood of their brethren).

blocks.text: Neither is it advisable to invoke Goddess Kali's blessings, Nor can her invocation be dispensed with for solving one's problems. Whosoever succeeds in satiating and appeasing the goddess, Ends up becoming an all powerful and mighty sovereign. (7)
lines: Neither is it advisable to invoke Goddess Kali's blessings,
Nor can her invocation be dispensed with for solving one's problems.
Whosoever succeeds in satiating and appeasing the goddess,
Ends up becoming an all powerful and mighty sovereign.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Since no body could invoke and satiate her in Kaliyuga, She devoured them since they failed to satiate her. I (Banda Singh) had intended to propitiate her through sacrifices of Singhs, But sparing the Singhs she had recoiled upon him instead. (8)
lines: Since no body could invoke and satiate her in Kaliyuga,
She devoured them since they failed to satiate her.
I (Banda Singh) had intended to propitiate her through sacrifices of Singhs,
But sparing the Singhs she had recoiled upon him instead.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Banda Singh instructed the (pleading) Singhs, That they should accomplish his (unfinished task). They must offer as many sacrifices of (living) heads, As remained in balance to square up the one lakh and a quarter figure. (9)
lines: Then Banda Singh instructed the (pleading) Singhs,
That they should accomplish his (unfinished task).
They must offer as many sacrifices of (living) heads,
As remained in balance to square up the one lakh and a quarter figure.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs, following the instructions of Banda Singh, Slaughtered all the horses and camels to meet that target. For the rest, they slaughtered all the dogs and cats, Which had gathered there to feed on the carcasses. (10)
lines: The Singhs, following the instructions of Banda Singh,
Slaughtered all the horses and camels to meet that target.
For the rest, they slaughtered all the dogs and cats,
Which had gathered there to feed on the carcasses.

blocks.text: Even then these sacrificial deaths fell short of the targetted figure, When the head count was taken for the promised figure. Then Banda Singh instructed the Singhs for more sacrifices, By killing houseflies to complete the figure of one lakh and a quarter. (11)
lines: Even then these sacrificial deaths fell short of the targetted figure,
When the head count was taken for the promised figure.
Then Banda Singh instructed the Singhs for more sacrifices,
By killing houseflies to complete the figure of one lakh and a quarter.

blocks.text: (After such ridiculous instructions), manypeople started feeling, As if Banda Singh lost his balance and had gone mad. While some followed Banda Singh's instruction in all sincerity, Others deserted his company feeling astonished at his wits. (12)
lines: (After such ridiculous instructions), manypeople started feeling,
As if Banda Singh lost his balance and had gone mad.
While some followed Banda Singh's instruction in all sincerity,
Others deserted his company feeling astonished at his wits.

blocks.text: The Singhs, who were devout, faithful and true to their salt, They declared to sacrifice their lives along with their leader. While some felt no justification in deserting their leader, Others deserted post haste without seeking anybody's advice. (13)
lines: The Singhs, who were devout, faithful and true to their salt,
They declared to sacrifice their lives along with their leader.
While some felt no justification in deserting their leader,
Others deserted post haste without seeking anybody's advice.

blocks.text: (As It Prevailed at Gurdaspur)
Dohra:

The most devout and faithful Singhs who chose to stay inside the fort, They had made a firm resolve (to sacrifice their lives). Since they considered every other option as undesirable, They preferred to embrace death than dishonour. (14)
lines: The most devout and faithful Singhs who chose to stay inside the fort,
They had made a firm resolve (to sacrifice their lives).
Since they considered every other option as undesirable,
They preferred to embrace death than dishonour.

blocks.text: Since hunger had reduced them to bare skeletons, They were gasping for breath (for want of food and water). While the Singhs were completely drained of energy and drive, The Mughals had almost entered their fortress. (15)
lines: Since hunger had reduced them to bare skeletons,
They were gasping for breath (for want of food and water).
While the Singhs were completely drained of energy and drive,
The Mughals had almost entered their fortress.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

After approaching quite near the Mughals laid a siege, And took positions behind the fort walls from all sides. (Dear readers) listen further to this tale of woeful deprivation, As it came to prevail inside this fort of Gurdas (Nangal). (16)
lines: After approaching quite near the Mughals laid a siege,
And took positions behind the fort walls from all sides.
(Dear readers) listen further to this tale of woeful deprivation,
As it came to prevail inside this fort of Gurdas (Nangal).

blocks.text: The moment somebody threw a morsel of bread from outside, The famished Singhs pounced upon it from every direction. Deprivation had effaced all distinctions between fair and foul means, As even the seniors snatched that morsel from their juniors to feed themselves. (17)
lines: The moment somebody threw a morsel of bread from outside,
The famished Singhs pounced upon it from every direction.
Deprivation had effaced all distinctions between fair and foul means,
As even the seniors snatched that morsel from their juniors to feed themselves.

blocks.text: Even if somebody threw the peelings from melons and honeydew inside, Tens of famished Singhs pounced upon that single peeling. If some body dangled a piece of bread from the floor, The starved Singhs would risk a fall from the roof to snatch it. (18)
lines: Even if somebody threw the peelings from melons and honeydew inside,
Tens of famished Singhs pounced upon that single peeling.
If some body dangled a piece of bread from the floor,
The starved Singhs would risk a fall from the roof to snatch it.

blocks.text: Food looked as rare as moon's first appearance in the waxing phase, Which disappears the moment one points one's finger towards it. Deprivation had driven the Singhs to such a miserable plight, That my pen (the poet's) fails to give expression to their misery. (19)
lines: Food looked as rare as moon's first appearance in the waxing phase,
Which disappears the moment one points one's finger towards it.
Deprivation had driven the Singhs to such a miserable plight,
That my pen (the poet's) fails to give expression to their misery.

blocks.text: Dohra:
So scared were the Mughal soldiers of Banda Singh, That they did not dare to step into his room. Lest he should still play a trick upon them, And from a scared cat might turn into a lion. (20)
lines: So scared were the Mughal soldiers of Banda Singh,
That they did not dare to step into his room.
Lest he should still play a trick upon them,
And from a scared cat might turn into a lion.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

They dared not go near Banda Singh, even though battered, As if the famished Banda would devour them. The Mughals were so much in dread of Banda Singh, As if a dead lion would get up to strangulate them. (21)
lines: They dared not go near Banda Singh, even though battered,
As if the famished Banda would devour them.
The Mughals were so much in dread of Banda Singh,
As if a dead lion would get up to strangulate them.

blocks.text: Such phantoms of fear of Banda Singh gripped the Mughals, As if more of Bandhayee Singhs would pounce upon them from nowhere.
Some opined that Banda Singh had prepared a boiling cauldron6 , In which Singhs would voluntarily sacrifice like the snakes. (22)
lines: Some opined that Banda Singh had prepared a boiling cauldron6 ,
In which Singhs would voluntarily sacrifice like the snakes.

blocks.text: Some apprehended that somebody might provide him with rations, After which Banda Singh would never fall into their hands. As a person, dying of thirst, chanced to get water, Became alert and energetic the moment his thirst was slaked. (23)
lines: Some apprehended that somebody might provide him with rations,
After which Banda Singh would never fall into their hands.
As a person, dying of thirst, chanced to get water,
Became alert and energetic the moment his thirst was slaked.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Like frogs which wither and shrink in size, In the extreme heat of month of June. But get revived and rejuvenated, The moment the monsoon rain sets in. (24)
lines: Like frogs which wither and shrink in size,
In the extreme heat of month of June.
But get revived and rejuvenated,
The moment the monsoon rain sets in.

blocks.text: The Mughals too entered into a variety of deliberations and confabulations, As they had several kinds of apprehensions about Banda Singh. They feared that other (Tat) Khalsa forces might join in a rally, And turn hostile and defiant even from inside the fort. (25)
lines: The Mughals too entered into a variety of deliberations and confabulations,
As they had several kinds of apprehensions about Banda Singh.
They feared that other (Tat) Khalsa forces might join in a rally,
And turn hostile and defiant even from inside the fort.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Mughals then resolved to reduce their numerical strength, By ousting them after subjecting them to severe beatings. They planned to capture Banda Singh after reducing their numerical strength, And despatch him to Delhi alive after capturing him. (26)
lines: The Mughals then resolved to reduce their numerical strength,
By ousting them after subjecting them to severe beatings.
They planned to capture Banda Singh after reducing their numerical strength,
And despatch him to Delhi alive after capturing him.

blocks.text: The Mughals, after resolving unanimously about this strategy, Opened one flank in order to facilitate their escape. Thereafter they made a public pronouncement there, That they were free to escape through that passage. (27)
lines: The Mughals, after resolving unanimously about this strategy,
Opened one flank in order to facilitate their escape.
Thereafter they made a public pronouncement there,
That they were free to escape through that passage.

blocks.text: Some people started fleeing leaving behind their weapons, As they had been devasted by extreme pangs of hunger. Only a small number of devout and faithful Singhs were left behind, Who kept lying flat leaving aside their weapons. (28)
lines: Some people started fleeing leaving behind their weapons,
As they had been devasted by extreme pangs of hunger.
Only a small number of devout and faithful Singhs were left behind,
Who kept lying flat leaving aside their weapons.

blocks.text: If somebody ventured to poke fun at them. They still retaliated angrily with tenfold intensity. The Majhail Singhs neither lowered the pitch of their defiance, Nor were they scared to get killed in war and fight. (29)
lines: If somebody ventured to poke fun at them.
They still retaliated angrily with tenfold intensity.
The Majhail Singhs neither lowered the pitch of their defiance,
Nor were they scared to get killed in war and fight.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As a burnt out rope did not shed its coiled shape, The Majhail Singhs did not shed their arrogance despite exhaustion. Their morale remained intact despite loss of energy to wield their weapons, Such was the mettle and fabric of these Majhail Singhs. (30)
lines: As a burnt out rope did not shed its coiled shape,
The Majhail Singhs did not shed their arrogance despite exhaustion.
Their morale remained intact despite loss of energy to wield their weapons,
Such was the mettle and fabric of these Majhail Singhs.

blocks.text: Why should they be scared of indulging in a fight, As they had already reached the end of their tether. Otherwise also they were not likely to be spared (by the enemy), As it was an open secret about their imminent end. (31)
lines: Why should they be scared of indulging in a fight,
As they had already reached the end of their tether.
Otherwise also they were not likely to be spared (by the enemy),
As it was an open secret about their imminent end.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

People were scared of their phantom figures of emaciated bodies, As if they had tumbled out and fleeing out of their graves. As all flesh had disappeared from their bones, It appeared as if dead bodies were struggling to breathe. (32)
lines: People were scared of their phantom figures of emaciated bodies,
As if they had tumbled out and fleeing out of their graves.
As all flesh had disappeared from their bones,
It appeared as if dead bodies were struggling to breathe.

blocks.text: It appeared as if dead corpses were made to walk, By sewing up these corpses by the hands of a magician. Each bone of their emaciated skeleton was transparently visible, And it seemed as if a single breath of air would blow them into air. (33)
lines: It appeared as if dead corpses were made to walk,
By sewing up these corpses by the hands of a magician.
Each bone of their emaciated skeleton was transparently visible,
And it seemed as if a single breath of air would blow them into air.

blocks.text: They appeared to be as light as paper mache articles, Which were likely to blow up at the first breath of air? Some spectators remarked that Singhs were no longer alive, As they had observed their emaciated bodies from a close range. (34)
lines: They appeared to be as light as paper mache articles,
Which were likely to blow up at the first breath of air?
Some spectators remarked that Singhs were no longer alive,
As they had observed their emaciated bodies from a close range.

blocks.text: They had become victims of such a worst catastrophe, That they had experienced death even before their death. The author's pen fails to give any further account of this incident, As this gory scene sends shivers down his spine . (35)
lines: They had become victims of such a worst catastrophe,
That they had experienced death even before their death.
The author's pen fails to give any further account of this incident,
As this gory scene sends shivers down his spine .

blocks.text: Nobody knew the mystery behind Banda Singh's survival, As nobody had ever noticed him taking feed or drop of water. He told that he was fasting if anybody enquired of him, As people had never seen him partaking anything. (36)
lines: Nobody knew the mystery behind Banda Singh's survival,
As nobody had ever noticed him taking feed or drop of water.
He told that he was fasting if anybody enquired of him,
As people had never seen him partaking anything.

blocks.text: Some people remarked that his captive spirits (Birs) fed him, While others believed he had mastered his bodily urges. Still others remarked that he had taken a dose of a herb, Which had satiated and eliminated his craving for food. (37)
lines: Some people remarked that his captive spirits (Birs) fed him,
While others believed he had mastered his bodily urges.
Still others remarked that he had taken a dose of a herb,
Which had satiated and eliminated his craving for food.
